info.description: Use OpenAI chat and Responses, generate or edit images, and create embeddings. Each tool exposes its current model and input options. Bind your own Ace Data Cloud credential privately as Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN in Authorization. Usage is billed to your account. Never place a token in chat or shared examples. Start: https://platform.acedata.cloud/?from=coze

n.description: The number of images to be generated ranges from 1 to 10. `dall-e-3` is fixed at `1`. The `dall-e-2`, `gpt-image-1` / `gpt-image-1.5` / `gpt-image-2` series, as well as the `nano-banana` / `nano-banana-2-lite` / `nano-banana-2` / `nano-banana-pro` series all support `n>1`: they will return and charge for the corresponding number of images. Note that `response_format=b64_json` only supports `n=1`, and for `n>1`, please use the default URL return. If some images fail to generate, only the successful parts will be returned and charged.

size.description: The size of the generated image is in the format `width x height`, or fill in `auto` to select the aspect ratio based on the prompt semantics. **`gpt-image-2`** accepts any `WIDTHxHEIGHT` value that conforms to the format, including 1K presets (`1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `1024x1536`, `1792x1024`, `1024x1792`), 2K presets (`2048x2048`, `2048x1536`, `1536x2048`, `2048x1152`, `1152x2048`), 4K presets (`2880x2880`, `3264x2448`, `2448x3264`, `3840x2160`, `2160x3840`), and any custom size; regardless of the size, each image is billed uniformly. Size restrictions: custom sizes must be multiples of 16, with the longer side not exceeding 3840, and total pixels not exceeding 8,294,400. `dall-e-2` supports: `256x256`, `512x512`, `1024x1024`. `dall-e-3` supports: `1024x1024`, `1792x1024`, `1024x1792`. When explicitly passing `auto`, the platform will determine based on clear pixels or ratios, naming standards (paper / print / platform ad / advertisement / device / photography / film), medium conventions, and composition in a sequential manner. In addition to common ratios, it can also retain non-standard ratios such as `1.91:1`, `1.85:1`, `2.39:1`, ISO paper `1:√2`, etc.; the result will be normalized to the service-supported multiples of 16 and pixel budget. If automatic judgment is unavailable, it will fall back to the model's default aspect ratio. Omitting the `size` field will directly use the model's default aspect ratio. If there are strict pixel requirements, please directly pass `WIDTHxHEIGHT`.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

model.description: Models for image generation. Supports OpenAI's `dall-e-2`, `dall-e-3`, `gpt-image-1` / `gpt-image-1.5` / `gpt-image-2` / `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` series, as well as Google's `nano-banana` / `nano-banana-2-lite` / `nano-banana-2` / `nano-banana-pro`. The parameters `size`, `quality`, `style`, `background`, `output_format`, `moderation`, and `response_format` supported by different models vary, please refer to the description of each field for details. `gpt-image-2` offers two optional suffix variants: `gpt-image-2:official` (official channel, stable and compliant, billed based on the actual Token usage for text input, image input, and image output) and `gpt-image-2:reverse` (equivalent to the default `gpt-image-2`, with a better cost-performance ratio).

style.description: The style of `dall-e-3`: `vivid` (hyper-realistic/dramatic) or `natural` (more naturally neutral).

prompt.description: Text description of the required image. The GPT image model supports up to 32,000 characters, `dall-e-2` supports up to 1,000 characters, and `dall-e-3` supports up to 4,000 characters. A selection of example prompts is provided in the dropdown list (source: [EvoLinkAI/awesome-gpt-image-2-prompts](https://github.com/EvoLinkAI/awesome-gpt-image-2-prompts), Apache-2.0 license); you can also enter your own.

quality.description: Image quality. GPT image model options: `auto` (default), `high`, `medium`, `low`. `dall-e-3` options: `hd` or `standard`. `dall-e-2` supports only: `standard`.

background.description: Set the background opacity for the GPT image model. The optional values are `transparent`, `opaque`, or `auto` (default). When selecting `transparent`, please use an output format that supports the Alpha channel (png/webp).

moderation.description: The content review levels of the GPT image model. `low` will relax the filtering strength; `auto` uses the default policy.

callback_url.description: Optional callback URL. Once provided, the API will immediately return `task_id` and will push the results to that URL via a POST request after the image generation is complete. The callback payload contains `task_id`, `trace_id`, `success` (boolean), and the complete response data or error information.

output_format.description: The return format of the GPT image model. Optional values are `png`, `jpeg`, or `webp`.

partial_images.description: The number of intermediate images sent during the streaming process (0-3). `0` indicates that the final image is returned directly in one event.

response_format.description: The return format for `dall-e-2` / `dall-e-3` images: `url` or `b64_json`. The GPT image model does not support this parameter (always returns base64 encoded).

output_compression.description: The compression level (0-100%) of the GPT image model when using `webp` or `jpeg` output formats.

post.description: Unified image generation endpoint compatible with the OpenAI Images API. A single endpoint supports DALL·E 2/3, the full GPT Image family (gpt-image-1, gpt-imag Full input requirements: https://platform.acedata.cloud/documents/openai-images-generations Submit once with async=true. Retain task_id and poll the matching task tool; a task ID is not a completed result. Do not resubmit while pending.

id.description: Task ID (returned in the original response). Used by `retrieve`.

type.description: Filter by task type. The same model may produce different task types depending on the actual processing path taken for this request, so it is not recommended to rely on the correspondence between type and model; omitting this field will return all types. Used by `retrieve_batch`.

action.description: Operation type. Use `retrieve` to query a single task, and use `retrieve_batch` to list tasks in bulk.

trace_id.description: The tracking ID of the original request. Used by `retrieve`.

count_mode.description: Counting mode. By default, `none` does not perform a full count and returns a provable quantity through pagination metadata; `exact` attempts to count the exact total within 2 seconds, and automatically degrades to a lower bound after timeout. Used by `retrieve_batch`.

created_at_max.description: Filter tasks created before this Unix timestamp (seconds). Used by `retrieve_batch`.

created_at_min.description: Filter tasks created after this Unix timestamp (seconds). Used by `retrieve_batch`.

post.summary: OpenAI Chat Completion API, compatible with the official API format.

id.description: The unique identifier for dialogue completion.

model.description: Model used for completing this conversation.

total_tokens.description: The total number of tokens used in this request (prompt + completion).

prompt_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the prompt.

completion_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the generated completion content.

audio_tokens.description: The number of audio input tokens in the prompt.

cached_tokens.description: The number of tokens hit in the cache in the prompt.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Details of token usage for prompts.

audio_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the audio output generated by the model.

reasoning_tokens.description: The number of tokens generated by the model for inference.

accepted_prediction_tokens.description: The number of tokens that appear in the completion of the predicted content when using predicted outputs.

rejected_prediction_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the predicted content that do not appear in the completion when using predicted outputs.

usage.description: Usage statistics for this completion request.

index.description: The index of the option in the list of options.

role.description: The role of the author of the message.

id.description: The unique identifier for the audio reply.

data.description: Base64 encoded audio bytes generated by the model.

expires_at.description: The audio reply is no longer available on the server (for multi-turn conversations) Unix timestamp (seconds).

transcript.description: Text transcription of audio generated by the model.

audio.description: When the audio output modality is requested, this object contains the audio response data returned by the model.

refusal.description: The message generated by the model rejecting the answer.

id.description: The ID of the tool call.

type.description: The type of tool invocation. Currently, only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to be called.

arguments.description: The parameters used when calling the function are generated by the model in JSON format.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls generated by the model, such as function calls.

message.description: A message completing a dialogue generated by the model.

logprobs.description: The logarithmic probability information of this option.

finish_reason.description: Reasons for the model to stop generating tokens. If the model reaches a natural stopping point or hits the provided stopping sequence, it is `stop`; if it reaches the maximum token number specified in the request, it is `length`; if content is omitted due to content filter flags, it is `content_filter`; if the model called a tool, it is `tool_calls`; if the model called a function (deprecated), it is `function_call`.

choices.description: Dialogue completion options list. If `n` is greater than 1, it may include multiple options.

created.description: Create the Unix timestamp (seconds) when this conversation is completed.

system_fingerprint.description: This fingerprint indicates the backend configuration used for the model run. It can be used in conjunction with the request parameter `seed` to understand when changes that may affect determinism occurred in the backend.

schema.description: Indicates a dialogue completion response returned by the model based on the provided input.

parameters.name: accept
parameters.description: Specify the response format returned by the server.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Bind your own Ace Data Cloud credential privately as Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN in Authorization. Usage is billed to your account. Never place a token in chat or shared examples.

n.description: Generate how many dialogue completion options for each input message.

seed.description: If specified, the system will strive to perform deterministic sampling, so that repeated requests using the same `seed` and parameters return the same results. Determinism cannot be guaranteed; please refer to the `system_fingerprint` in the response to monitor backend changes.

stop.description: A maximum of 4 sequences, the API will stop generating when it reaches these sequences. The returned text does not include the stopping sequences.

user.description: A unique identifier representing your end users, which helps the platform monitor and detect abusive behavior.

voice.description: The tone used by the model in its responses.

audio.description: Audio output parameters. Required when requesting audio output via `modalities: ["audio"]`.

store.description: Whether to store the output of this conversation completion request for model distillation or product evaluation.

type.description: Type of tool. Currently only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to be called.

parameters.description: The parameters accepted by this function are described by a JSON Schema object.

tools.description: List of tools that can be called by the model. Currently, only functions are supported as tools.

top_p.description: An alternative method for temperature sampling, called nucleus sampling, considers only the portion of tokens whose cumulative probability mass reaches top_p. For example, 0.1 means only considering the tokens that account for the top 10% of cumulative probability mass. It is generally recommended to adjust only one of these parameters or `temperature`, rather than adjusting both simultaneously.

stream.description: Use false for Coze JSON tool results.

logprobs.description: Whether to return the logarithmic probability of the output tokens. If true, it will return the logarithmic probability of each output token in the `content` of `message`.

name.description: Optional names for participants. Used to provide information to the model to distinguish different participants under the same role.

url.description: The URL of the image, or Base64 encoded image data.

detail.description: Specify the detail level of the image.

image_url.description: Image URL or Base64 encoded image data.

type.description: The type of the content part is fixed as `input_audio`.

format.description: The format for encoding audio data. Currently supports `wav` and `mp3`.

input_audio.description: Audio data sent to the model.

file_id.description: The ID of the uploaded file used as input.

filename.description: Filename, used to pass the file to the model in string form.

file_data.description: Base64 encoded file data, used when passing the file as a string to the model.

file.description: File data sent to the model.

type.description: The type of the content part is fixed as `file`.

oneOf.description: An array composed of content parts with explicit types, which can include input types such as text, image_url, input_audio, and file.

content.description: The content of the message. Plain text messages can be in string format, while multimodal messages (containing text, image_url, input_audio, and file) can be in the form of an array of content parts.

refusal.description: The assistant's refusal to answer message. Use when `role` is `assistant`.

id.description: The ID of the tool call.

type.description: Type of tool. Currently only supports `function`.

name.description: The name of the function to be called.

arguments.description: The parameters used when calling the function are generated by the model in JSON format.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls generated by the model in the previous round (when `role` is `assistant`). Please return it along with the `tool` message that contains the results of the tool call.

tool_call_id.description: The tool call that responds to this message. It is required when the role is `tool`.

messages.description: List of messages that make up the current conversation.

metadata.description: A set of key-value pairs that can be attached to an object, with a maximum of 16 pairs. It can be used to store additional information about the object in a structured format. The key is a string of up to 64 characters, and the value is a string of up to 512 characters.

logit_bias.description: Modify the likelihood of a specified token appearing in the completion. Accept a JSON object that maps the token (specified by its token ID in the tokenizer) to a bias value between -100 and 100.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in dialogue completion.

modalities.description: You hope for the output type generated by the model. Most models default to `["text"]`. The `gpt-4o-audio-preview` model can also be used to generate audio. If you want the model to generate both text and audio responses, you can use `["text", "audio"]`.

type.description: Predict the type of content, fixed as `content`.

prediction.description: Static prediction output content, such as the content of a text file that is being regenerated. It can be used to shorten response time when most of the response content is already known in advance.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature used ranges from 0 to 2. Higher values (such as 0.8) will make the output more random, while lower values (such as 0.2) will make the output more focused and certain.

oneOf.description: Control which tool the model calls (if any).

type.description: Type of tool. Currently only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to be called.

oneOf.description: Specify the tools that the designated model should use.

tool_choice.description: Control which tool the model calls (if any). `none` means the model will not call any tools; `auto` means the model can choose between generating a message or calling one/multiple tools; `required` means the model must call one or more tools.

service_tier.description: Specify the processing type used for the designated service request. Set to `auto` to let the platform choose automatically, `default` for standard pricing/performance, `flex` for a slower but cheaper Flex processing layer, and `priority` for the fastest processing layer on supported models.

top_logprobs.description: The integer value between 0 and 20 specifies the number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each accompanied by the corresponding log probability. When using this parameter, `logprobs` must be set to `true`.

include_usage.description: If set, an additional chunk will be streamed back before the `data: [DONE]` message. The `usage` field of this chunk displays the total token usage statistics for the entire request, while the `choices` field will always be an empty array.

stream_options.description: Options for streaming responses. Use only when setting `stream: true`.

oneOf.description: JSON Object response format. The model must be instructed to output JSON in the prompt.

type.description: Enable structured outputs to ensure that the model's output matches the provided JSON Schema.

name.description: The name of the response format. It can only contain a-z, A-Z, 0-9, underscores, and hyphens.

schema.description: The schema of the response format is described using a JSON Schema object.

strict.description: Whether to enable strict schema adherence.

description.description: Description of the purpose of this response format.

oneOf.description: Use the structured output response format of JSON Schema.

response_format.description: The object format that the specified model must output. Setting it to `{ "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...} }` enables structured output; setting it to `{ "type": "json_object" }` enables the older JSON Object mode.

presence_penalty.description: The value ranges from -2.0 to 2.0. Positive values will penalize based on whether the token has already appeared in the generated text, thereby increasing the model's likelihood of discussing new topics.

reasoning_effort.description: The inference input level of the constraint reasoning model (o1/o3/o4/gpt-5 series). Currently supports `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, and `high`. Reducing the inference input can lead to faster responses and decrease the number of tokens used for inference in the responses.

frequency_penalty.description: The value ranges from -2.0 to 2.0. Positive values will penalize based on the frequency of the token appearing in the generated text, thereby reducing the likelihood of the model repeating the same line word for word.

search_context_size.description: High-level guidelines on the size of the context window space occupied by the search.

web_search_options.description: Options for web search tools, for use with the GPT-4o model that has built-in search (`gpt-4o-search-preview`, `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview`).

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether to enable parallel function calls during tool invocation.

max_completion_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens that can be generated for a single completion, including visible output tokens and inference tokens. For newer models (o1/o3/o4/gpt-5 series and other inference models), this parameter replaces `max_tokens`.

parameters.name: accept
parameters.description: Specify the response format, only supporting `application/json`.

parameters.name: Content-Type
parameters.description: Use `multipart/form-data` to upload image files, or use `application/json` to reference images via URL (extended mode; JSON mode does not support direct upload of file bytes).

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Bind your own Ace Data Cloud credential privately as Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN in Authorization. Usage is billed to your account. Never place a token in chat or shared examples.

n.description: Number of images to generate (1-10). `dall-e-3` is fixed at `1`. The `dall-e-2`, `gpt-image-1` / `gpt-image-1.5` / `gpt-image-2` series, as well as the `nano-banana` / `nano-banana-2-lite` / `nano-banana-2` / `nano-banana-pro` series all support `n>1`: they will return and charge for the corresponding number of edited results. Note that `response_format=b64_json` only supports `n=1`, for `n>1` please use the default URL return. If some images fail to generate, only the successful parts will be returned and charged.

size.description: Image size, in the format of `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, or `auto`. **`gpt-image-2`** accepts any `WIDTHxHEIGHT` value that conforms to this format, including 1K presets (`1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `1024x1536`, `1792x1024`, `1024x1792`), 2K presets (`2048x2048`, `2048x1536`, `1536x2048`, `2048x1152`, `1152x2048`), 4K presets (`2880x2880`, `3264x2448`, `2448x3264`, `3840x2160`, `2160x3840`), and custom sizes; regardless of the size, each image is billed at a fixed price. Size limitations: custom sizes must be multiples of 16, with the long side ≤ 3840, and total pixel count ≤ 8,294,400. `dall-e-2` supports: `256x256`, `512x512`, `1024x1024`. When passing `auto` (default) or leaving it blank, the output will maintain the aspect ratio of the reference image; if the aspect ratio needs to be changed, `WIDTHxHEIGHT` must be explicitly specified.

async.description: Whether to process in asynchronous mode. When set to `true`, the interface immediately returns `task_id`, without the need to provide `callback_url`, and then the result can be obtained by polling the corresponding task query interface; if `callback_url` is also provided, the result will be pushed to that callback address.

image.description: Reference image URL. Accepts a single URL string or an array of URL strings (up to 16 for the GPT Image series models, `dall-e-2` supports only 1). The JSON mode **does not** accept uploaded file bytes—if you need to upload files directly, please use `multipart/form-data`.

model.description: Models used for image editing. Supports `dall-e-2`, `dall-e-3`, GPT Image series (`gpt-image-1`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`) as well as Google Nano Banana series (`nano-banana`, `nano-banana-2-lite`, `nano-banana-2`, `nano-banana-pro`). `gpt-image-2` offers two optional suffix variants: `gpt-image-2:official` (official channel, stable and compliant, billed based on actual Token usage for text input, image input, and image output) and `gpt-image-2:reverse` (equivalent to the default `gpt-image-2`, with a better cost-performance ratio).

prompt.description: Describe the text of the desired editing effect. `dall-e-2` up to 1000 characters, GPT Image series models up to 32000 characters.

quality.description: Image quality. The GPT Image series models support: `auto`, `high`, `medium`, `low`.

background.description: Only applicable to the GPT Image series models. Transparency handling methods: `transparent` (transparent), `opaque` (opaque), or `auto` (automatic).

callback_url.description: Optional callback URL. When provided, the interface immediately returns `task_id` and pushes the results to that URL via POST after the image editing is completed.

output_format.description: The return formats of the GPT Image series models are: `png`, `jpeg`, or `webp`.

input_fidelity.description: Matching strength of style and features of the input image (applicable to GPT Image series models).

post.description: OpenAI image editing API, input images and instructions, output modified images. Full input requirements: https://platform.acedata.cloud/documents/openai-images-edits Submit once with async=true. Retain task_id and poll the matching task tool; a task ID is not a completed result. Do not resubmit while pending.
